profile.headline: Software Engineer
profile.summary: I am a software developer since 2011. I have experience developing software in Python, C, C++, C#, Assembly Language, JavaScript, Java, PHP, MySQL, PostgreSQL, and Visual Basic. I have worked on various IT solutions in the field of business, education, and health. In addition to my software engineering expertise, I developed diverse sets of interpersonal, organizational, and public speaking skills through my teaching experience.

positions.title: Assistant Lecturer
positions.description: Despite my title, I also served as a software developer for IPRC Tumba; former Tumba College of Technology. I contributed to developing a Student Information Management that served as a students' registration platform as well as a centralized student records database.

positions.title: Graduate Teaching Assistant
positions.description: I served as a graduate teaching assistant for Linux and Programming.

positions.title: Graduate Teaching Assistant
positions.description:
I serve as a graduate teaching assistant for Advanced Database System, where I work closely with the lecturer to conduct practical sessions.
The course covers Transactional Systems, Concurrency Control, Active Database, and NoSQL Databases. In addition to that, I deliver recitation on material covered and help students to understand the assignments. As the course aims to describe the databases in a way suitable for applications and computer systems designers, databases such as PostgreSQL and MongoDB are covered.

projects.title: <Test Automation Platform />
projects.description:
As a full-stack engineer for a Test Automation Platform, I was pivotal in engineering a fully functioning dashboard to monitor the metrics, status, and automated tests of IoT-connected devices.
My responsibilities included creating a VueJS dashboard that dynamically pulled data from AWS services, including API Gateway, S3, and Cloudwatch. This cloud-native project leveraged multiple AWS services that were provisioned and managed through AWS CDK and integrated into an automated CI/CD pipeline.

projects.title: Faulty Product Detection and Separation System
projects.description:
This project was completed as part of the effort for the Embedded Systems course taken at Carnegie Mellon University.

The goal of the project was to design a system that would detect defective products on the conveyor belt. I used an ultrasonic range detector connected to the WSP-WROOM-32 microcontroller to detect boxes of imperfect sizes.

The microcontroller was counting the total number of containers, together with the total number of defected ones, with a dashboard displaying real-time statistics on the production performance from the data saved on the cloud.
